from collections import Counter as C2
inp={k:G[f'Demo pair {k} input'] for k in range(1,7)}
outs={k:G[f'Demo pair {k} output'] for k in range(1,7)}
# d6 out = middle row only. Markers per block [[1,3,2],[2,5,5],[1,2,3]]. Middle row marked. What distinguishes middle row? counts 2..9 vs corners 1,1... 
# Maybe rule: mark iff block count ODD considering only colors of SECOND-bg type? For d6 second bg=2. Count of color2 per block: [[2,6,4],[2,4,2],[2,5,2]]. odd: (1,2),(2,1)... no.
# New angle: maybe the rule uses SUM over blocks of color c across rows/cols: e.g., mark (a,b) iff number of cells of color c IN THE WHOLE GRID within column-band b... too speculative. Instead check d1/d4 identical outs and d3/d5 identical outs — maybe the inputs are noisy copies of a hidden pattern and the OUTPUT reveals the pattern via voting across demos?? No, each demo is independent.
# Check: in each demo, does the input contain an exact repeatable 3x3 subgrid scaled x~2.33, i.e., a motif repeated at scale... The out patterns (zigzag, T) look like letters? 'F'? zigzag could be digit. Perhaps output = the shape formed by the LEAST common color when its cells are connected and you take bounding box normalized to 3x3!
for n in range(1,7):
    I_=inp[n]; o=outs[n]
    cnt=C2(x for r in I_ for x in r); bgs=sorted(cnt.most_common(2))[::2] or [v for v,_ in cnt.most_common(2)]
    # rarest color(s)
    rare=min(((c,v) for v,c in cnt.items()),key=lambda x:x[1])[1]
    pos=[(i,j) for i in range(7) for j in range(7) if I_[i][j]==rare]
    r0=min(p[0] for p in pos); r1=max(p[0] for p in pos)+1; c0=min(p[1] for p in pos); c1=max(p[1] for p in pos)+1
    h=r1-r0; w=c1-c0
    m=[[0]*3 for _ in range(3)]
    for i,j in pos:
        aa=(i-r0)*(2)//h if h>=2 else 0; bb=(j-c0)*(2)//w if w>=2 else 0
        m[aa][bb]=1
    ok=m==[[o[a][b]!=0 for b in range(3)] for a in range(3)]
    print('demo',n,'rarest',rare,len(pos),'shape',m,'match',ok,'out',[o[a][b]!=0 for a in range(3) for b in range(3)])
